title: Console walkthrough: usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown
summary: Redwood AE & SE walked Apex Retail through the Console usage analytics and per-route dashboards, focusing on token-level cost breakdowns and routing policies. Customer asked about VPC/private options, SOC2/KMS, and a benchmark pilot. Agreed next steps: pricing + cost spreadsheet, security docs, and a benchmark with sample traffic.
next_steps: Maya to send pricing deck + per-route cost spreadsheet
Liam to share benchmark plan and availability for week of Apr 5
Jordan to send sample traffic logs and SLO targets
Schedule legal/ procurement intro if pilot approved
action_items: Maya Patel: Send pricing + per-route cost spreadsheet (due 2026-04-01)
Liam Chen: Prepare benchmark plan and run initial throughput test (due 2026-04-07)
Jordan Miles: Share sample traffic, retention and SLOs (due 2026-04-02)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-29 14:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Miles (Apex Retail - Head of ML), Priya Rao (Apex - Platform Eng), Carlos Medina (Apex - CTO)

Summary: quick console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown; customer wants clarity on per-route cost attribution and options for private deployment.

[00:00] Maya: okay hey everyone, thanks for joining uh super excited to show the Console analytics today, can you all hear me ok?
[00:08] Jordan: yes, loud and clear, thanks Maya.
[00:12] Maya: quick intro I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood team, and Liam is our solutions engineer, he'll walk through the console and the live dashboards.
[00:20] Liam: hi all, quick background - i'll show per-route dashboards, token level cost, model routing, and a short bit on Optimize recommendations.
[00:30] Priya: our main ask is understanding how to attribute cost to product teams and to see spikes by route and model, and whether we can export that data.
[00:40] Liam: yup, that's exactly what the usage analytics are for. starting at the overview page, you get top level token usage, cost, and p50/p95 latency by model.
[00:50] [00:50] (screen share) Liam: here's the per-route table; you can filter by time, model, and deployment (hosted vs dedicated). Notice we compute token counts and estimated dollars using your pricing profile.
[01:15] Jordan: question - is that estimate based on our contract pricing or standard hosted pricing?
[01:22] Maya: for demos it's using the hosted rate, but when we set up a dedicated account we sync your commit/discounts so the per-route cost matches invoicing.
[01:30] Priya: can we export per-route cost as CSV or into our BI tools?
[01:35] Liam: yes, export CSV and direct S3 export are both available; we also have an API endpoint to pull per-route metrics.
[01:45] Carlos: how granular are the route tags? can we tag calls by product feature?
[01:50] Liam: you can tag routes at the SDK or API level: route name, team tags, environment. The dashboard supports grouping by tag.
[02:05] [02:05] Jordan: okay that's helpful. on security - we're regulated and need SOC2 plus KMS integration, and ideally VPC/private deployment.
[02:12] Maya: understood. we have SOC2 attestation; we also offer Private deployment with customer VPC and KMS/HSM integrations. i'll share the security FAQ after this.
[02:25] Priya: for Private, how different is the console - are the analytics still the same?
[02:30] Liam: console is the same interface; for Private deployment the control plane is customer-controlled or a private control plane and metrics are ingested back into the console via secure connectors. some integrations require an initial setup with our infra team.
[02:50] [03:00] Jordan: curious about model routing - can we route cheaper models for low-latency things and keep high-quality models for edge cases?
[03:08] Liam: yes, we support policy-based routing - route by latency SLO, cost threshold, or fallback to a cheaper quantized model. the per-route dashboard shows you what percent of requests hit each model.
[03:25] (Liam clicks into a per-route breakdown)
[03:30] Liam: here, this route is 70% on redwood-llm-3-small and 30% on r-llm-4 for complex prompts; you can see cost per request and tokens.
[03:45] Jordan: small transcription note - did you say 'redwood-llm-3-small' or 'redwood lm three small', transcription is fuzzy but we got it.
[03:52] Liam: yeah redwood-llm-3-small, and r-llm-4 is our higher-quality option.
[04:05] [04:05] Maya: i'd like to highlight the anomaly detection - we show sudden token spikes and attribute to route+prompt length, useful for catching noisy front-end behavior.
[04:20] Priya: do you show model warmup or KV cache hit rates? that impacts our latency and cost.
[04:26] Liam: yes, we surface KV cache hit %, average sequence length, and batching efficiency. those metrics feed into Optimize suggestions.
[04:45] Jordan: can Optimize recommend quantization levels per model and estimate delta in latency/cost?
[04:52] Liam: Optimize runs a profile and suggests quantization and batching settings with estimated throughput/latency and expected cost savings; we include a projected quality delta and run evals against your prompt set.
[05:15] [05:15] Carlos: procurement question - if we commit to Dedicated, what's the process to get per-route quotas and dedicated capacity?
[05:22] Maya: Dedicated is via reserved capacity contracts; we size GPU pools based on your traffic profile. Liam usually runs a sizing benchmark and we present options for commit tiers.
[05:35] Jordan: we'd like a benchmark with our sample traffic.
[05:38] Maya: great — Liam can run that. we'll need sample traces and SLOs.
[05:45] Liam: I'll draft a benchmark plan after the call and propose dates, aiming for week of Apr 5.
[05:52] [06:00] (silent typing / screen)
[06:10] Liam: back to the console — here's the cost waterfall view: model compute, tokenization, networking, and caching credits. you can hover to see which model or route contributed.
[06:30] Priya: networking — if we run Private in our VPC, is networking cost shown separately?
[06:36] Liam: networking costs are shown as a line item; for Private deployments we can optionally omit network egress from Redwood billing and let you report it in your cloud bills.
[06:50] Jordan: any limits on retention for logs and analytics?
[06:54] Maya: default retention is 90 days; extended retention and raw data exports are add-ons.
[07:05] [07:05] Priya: curious about token attribution for multi-tool responses — if we call a tool, does the token cost go to the original route?
[07:12] Liam: tokens are attributed to the initiating route; tools calls are broken out in the detailed view so you can see tool vs model cost.
[07:28] Jordan: nice. for billing alignment we need route->cost mapping to our internal teams weekly. can Redwood push that automatically?
[07:35] Maya: yes, we can configure scheduled exports to S3 and set up webhooks to push metrics to your billing pipeline.
[07:45] [08:00] (15 minute mark summary)
[08:05] Maya: quick recap of the first chunk - per-route dashboards support filtering, exports, tagging; Optimize gives quantization and batching recommendations; security and Private options exist and Liam will follow up on benchmarks.
[08:20] Jordan: sounds good.
[08:25] [08:30] Liam: i'll show a demo of the anomaly detection alert rule creation — you can set a rule on tokens per minute and have it trigger pagerduty or a slack webhook.
[08:45] (Liam creates an alert)
[09:00] Priya: can we attach the actual log snippet to the alert?
[09:04] Liam: yes the alert includes a link to the last 100 requests for that window.
[09:12] Jordan: on the segmentation view — can we break down by customer_id hashed? we don't want raw PII.
[09:18] Liam: yes we support hashing/obfuscation; you can configure which fields to hash before ingest so analytics keep identifiers but no raw PII.
[09:30] [10:00] Maya: switching to the per-model cost trend — you can compare model A vs B over 30/90 days and see cost per 1k tokens.
[10:15] Priya: do you surface effective throughput vs provisioned GPU utilization for Dedicated?
[10:20] Liam: yes, utilization metrics are shown. we also show queue lengths and average waiting time when autoscaling occurred.
[10:35] Jordan: what about demos we saw earlier about fallback policies, if dedicated runs out of capacity do we automatically route to hosted?
[10:42] Liam: we support fallback policies - route to hosted or a smaller model; you can set rules per-route for graceful degradation.
[11:00] [11:00] Carlos: legal question - retention of logs for audits, can Redwood provide audit logs for model changes and rollouts?
[11:08] Maya: yes, we provide audit trails, rollouts history, and signing for deploy events. we'll include that in the security pack.
[11:20] Jordan: any references to competitors we should be aware of? we looked at Anthropic and some self-hosted approaches.
[11:27] Maya: common. we differentiate on unified console and strong per-route analytics tied to cost controls.
[11:40] [12:00] (mid-call)
[12:05] Liam: showing the 'cost drilldown' for a high-traffic route — see how a long prompt and repeated retries spiked cost last week.
[12:20] Priya: can we set up synthetic traffic to validate cost changes?
[12:24] Liam: yes, we can run synthetic traffic in a sandbox; that's part of the benchmark plan.
[12:35] Jordan: for the pilot, we want an initial 2-week trial with our staging traffic and then scale.
[12:40] Maya: noted. we'll propose pilot terms in the follow-up.
[12:50] [13:00] (small crosstalk)
[13:10] Liam: quick note on accuracy - Optimize gives you an estimated "quality delta" when suggesting quantization; we also run evals against your prompt set to quantify the impact.
[13:25] Jordan: how long are those evals typically?
[13:28] Liam: depends on set size; 500\u20132k prompts usually takes a few hours on our infra.
[13:40] Priya: if we want on-premise, what's the timeline?
[13:45] Maya: on-prem typically 8\u201312 weeks for full deployment including security reviews and network setup. VPC-private is faster, usually 2\u20134 weeks.
[13:58] [15:00] (15 minute checkpoint)
[15:05] Carlos: can you break out a sample invoice showing per-route lines?
[15:10] Maya: yes i will attach a sample invoice with line items by route and model.
[15:18] Jordan: great.
[15:25] [16:00] (demo continues)
[16:10] Liam: jumping to the API access — you can query the /analytics endpoint to pull cost per route and per model. here's a curl example.
[16:25] Priya: will the API support fine-grained time buckets? we need 5-minute granularity.
[16:30] Liam: yes, 1m, 5m, 15m buckets are all supported.
[16:40] Jordan: for our finance team, could you map route tags to GL codes automatically?
[16:45] Maya: we can set up a mapping during onboarding and push mapped exports weekly.
[17:00] [18:00] (deep dive into Optimize)
[18:10] Liam: Optimize suggests batching sizes, cache TTLs and model quantization per workload; it also estimates dollars saved and expected latency change.
[18:25] Jordan: curious about safety - if we change quantization, do we need to re-run safety evals?
[18:30] Liam: we recommend re-running evals for safety-sensitive workloads; Optimize can re-run a subset of safety prompts as part of the suggestion.
[18:45] Priya: can we lock the rollout so only certain teams can approve quantization changes?
[18:50] Maya: yes RBAC controls and rollout approvals exist in Console.
[19:05] [20:00] (20m mark)
[20:10] Jordan: procurement timeline - if the pilot looks good, we want a month-long PO process with our legal.
[20:17] Maya: understood; i'll loop in our sales ops.
[20:25] Carlos: any gotchas with cloud provider egress billing?
[20:30] Liam: egress is billed by the cloud provider; we surface network egress in the console and you can choose to exclude it from Redwood billing for Private.
[20:45] [22:00] (closing demo)
[22:10] Liam: final checklist - exports, alerts, per-route tags, Optimize recommendations, benchmark plan.
[22:20] Maya: next steps - i'll send pricing and security docs; Liam will share benchmark plan. Jordan will share traffic sample.
[22:30] Jordan: thanks all. quick note - we did mention Anthropic and host vs self-host options in our evaluation.
[22:38] Maya: thanks for the context - we'll tailor the proposal.
[22:45] [23:00] (wrap)
[23:05] Maya: recap of action items: pricing + per-route spreadsheet, SOC2 + KMS docs, benchmark plan for week of Apr 5, sample traffic from Jordan.
[23:20] Priya: thanks everyone, good session.
[23:30] Carlos: bye.

(Transcription note: occasional mis-hearings for model names and internal tags, but overall captures key asks and next steps.)
